inlines.text: Providence Swedish Cancer Institute 胸部肿瘤临床与研究项目医学主任 Sid Devarakonda 博士研究肺癌为何发生、为何产生耐药。他的研究很大一部分是分析肿瘤的 DNA 和 RNA，以探究临床中观察到的现象。比如，患者对某种治疗出现了意料之外的反应，这就可以成为一个问题，到数据中去寻找答案。

blocks.text: Devarakonda 与我们 Asta 团队合作，开始测试 Theorizer——一个 AI 智能体，它把科学论文中的发现综合起来，为肿瘤不明原因生长这类观察提出解释。Devarakonda 审阅它给出的第一批理论时，认出了自己多年研究形成的想法。他回忆说，第二天他心想：“等等，这正是我的想法。而我花了 15 年才想到这一步。”

blocks.text: 今天，我们在 Asta 中推出 Theorizer。Asta 是我们面向科学研究的 AI 智能体平台，同时我们开源了代码，研究者可以查看它如何生成理论，并把方法调整后用于自己的工作。通过 Asta 的网页界面使用，我们承担一定额度内的 token 费用；更愿意在自己的机器上运行的人，可以使用我们的开源库，按需支付 token 费用。

blocks.text: 研究肺癌

inlines.text: 研究肺癌

blocks.text: Devarakonda 用 Theorizer 研究“驱动基因阴性”肺腺癌，这是肺癌中最常见的亚型。大多数肺腺癌带有若干种基因改变之一，这些改变会激活 RAS 通路——一条促进细胞生长的信号链。但在约 20% 到 30% 的病例中，即使做了全面测序，也找不到已知的驱动基因改变。为了弄清是什么让这些细胞不断增殖，Devarakonda 问 Theorizer：“这些肿瘤里发生了什么？”

blocks.text: Theorizer 会针对用户的问题检索研究文献，然后生成一个模板，规定从每篇论文中提取哪些内容。对于肺癌如何生长这类问题，模板可能包括：一项研究考察了哪些基因、研究者如何测量这些基因的活性，以及研究者改变这些基因后发生了什么。Theorizer 比较提取出的发现来生成理论，并把论点与背后的论文关联起来。研究者可以查看所引用的研究，评估某个理论得到的支持，以及这些研究考察的条件是否可比。该工具还会标出它认为属于新提出的论点，但检索可能漏掉更早的工作，模型也可能误判原创性；研究者仍需对照更广泛的文献核实某个论点。

blocks.text: 经过多轮迭代，Theorizer 帮助 Devarakonda 提出了三种假说，解释肺腺癌肿瘤在没有已知驱动基因的情况下如何生长。第一种是某个未被检测到的基因改变激活了 RAS 信号通路；第二种是另一种机制让细胞不依赖 RAS 也能分裂；第三种是部分肿瘤获得了其他细胞类型的特征，不再表现出典型肺腺癌的行为。Theorizer 帮助他那个关于肿瘤不明原因生长的宽泛问题，转化为可以在分子数据中逐一检验的具体假说。

blocks.text: Devarakonda 和 Asta 团队用 AutoDiscovery 验证这些理论。这个工具能编写并运行代码，用数据集检验假说。Devarakonda 利用癌症基因组图谱（一个公开的肿瘤分子数据集合），比较有已知驱动基因和无已知驱动基因的癌症在基因改变、基因活性和蛋白质测量上的差异。他还分析了实验室培养的癌细胞数据，找出生长或存活所必需的基因。

blocks.text: AutoDiscovery 提出，DREAM 复合体的紊乱可能有助于解释这些肿瘤的生长。DREAM 复合体是一组通常抑制细胞分裂的蛋白质。Devarakonda 起初并没有关注这一机制。他与 Asta 团队合作，比较了 RAS 活性与该复合体通常调控的基因的开启强度。

blocks.text: 利用实验室培养的癌细胞数据开展的后续工作，为 Devarakonda 的假说提供了初步支持：一些 RAS 活性较低的癌症可能依赖 CDK2，这是一种参与细胞分裂的蛋白质。如果这些细胞确实依赖 CDK2，那么阻断该蛋白或许能减缓或阻止其生长。

blocks.text: 研究脑细胞功能

inlines.text: 研究脑细胞功能

blocks.text: Allen 研究所副研究员 Jérôme Lecoq 开发神经记录方法，用于研究小鼠的脑活动。他参与 OpenScope 项目，这是一个共享实验平台，研究人员通过它向 Allen 研究所提出神经科学研究方案，由研究所负责实施，所得数据集向全球研究人员公开共享。

inlines.text: Allen 研究所副研究员 Jérôme Lecoq 开发神经记录方法，用于研究小鼠的脑活动。他参与 OpenScope 项目，这是一个共享实验平台，研究人员通过它向 Allen 研究所提出神经科学研究方案，由研究所负责实施，所得数据集向全球研究人员公开共享。

blocks.text: Lecoq 在 VIP 中间神经元上评估了 Theorizer 的早期版本。VIP 中间神经元是抑制其他神经元活动的一类脑细胞，其目标包括通常抑制周围回路活动的抑制性细胞；抑制这些细胞，可以让附近的神经元反应更强。

inlines.text: 秘鲁气候数据中的异常

blocks.text: 在秘鲁的国际马铃薯中心（CIP），数据科学家兼统计专家 Piero Palacios 开发工具，帮助研究人员分析复杂数据集。CIP 的系统与数据管理官员 Henry Juarez 从事农业数据工作，并研究本土马铃薯品种的保护。

inlines.text: 在秘鲁的国际马铃薯中心（CIP），数据科学家兼统计专家 Piero Palacios 开发工具，帮助研究人员分析复杂数据集。CIP 的系统与数据管理官员 Henry Juarez 从事农业数据工作，并研究本土马铃薯品种的保护。

blocks.text: Palacios 和 Juarez 希望延长 PISCO 中的露点记录。PISCO 是一个利用气象站观测数据估算秘鲁各地气候状况的数据集。更长的记录可以为农业模型补上缺失的输入，包括用来估算作物需水量的模型。

blocks.text: PISCO 的露点记录止于 2016 年，而最低气温记录延续到 2020 年。Palacios 和 Juarez 利用重叠的历史数据估算缺失四年的露点，但一些重建值超过 35°C——对受影响地区来说，这样的日露点高得不合常理——而且集中在 11 月。

blocks.text: “桌面上有一个具体、可证伪的机制，正是推动我们按与历史记录中气象站的距离来测量 11 月峰值的原因，”Palacios 和 Juarez 说，“在异常只是无法解释的时候，我们本来没有特别理由做这项分析，而正是这项分析得出了真正的答案。”

inlines.text: Vilma Hualla 是 CIP 的数据管理专家，研究安第斯地区原生马铃薯品种的多样性。她和同事正在梳理秘鲁库斯科大区 Paucartambo 地区跨越一个世纪的历史记录和家庭调查。

blocks.text: Hualla 用 AutoDiscovery 比较了六个时期记录的品种。在大多数时期更替中，进入记录的品种多于消失的品种，但 1941–60 年到 1961–80 年的过渡是个例外：从记录中消失的品种多于首次出现的品种。

blocks.text: Investigating lung cancer

inlines.text: Investigating lung cancer

blocks.text: Devarakonda used Theorizer to investigate “driver-negative” lung adenocarcinoma, the most common subtype of lung cancer. Most lung adenocarcinomas have one of several genetic alterations that activate the RAS pathway, a chain of signals that promotes cell growth. But in roughly 20% to 30% of cases, even comprehensive sequencing does not reveal a recognized driver alteration. To understand what keeps the cells multiplying, Devarakonda asked Theorizer, “What’s happening in these tumors?”

inlines.text: Devarakonda used Theorizer to investigate “driver-negative” lung adenocarcinoma, the most common subtype of lung cancer. Most lung adenocarcinomas have one of several genetic alterations that activate the RAS pathway, a chain of signals that promotes cell growth. But in roughly 20% to 30% of cases, even comprehensive sequencing does not reveal a recognized driver alteration. To understand what keeps the cells multiplying, Devarakonda asked Theorizer, “What’s happening in these tumors?”

blocks.text: Theorizer searches the research literature in response to a user’s question, then creates a template specifying what to extract from each paper. For a question about how lung cancers grow, that might include which genes a study examined, how researchers measured their activity, and what happened when the researchers altered those genes. Theorizer compares the extracted findings to generate theories, linking claims to the papers behind them. Researchers can inspect the cited studies to assess the support for a theory and whether the studies examined comparable conditions. The tool also flags claims it considers new, but a search can miss earlier work and the model can misjudge originality; researchers still need to check a claim against the wider literature.

blocks.text: After several iterations, Theorizer helped Devarakonda formulate three hypotheses for how lung adenocarcinoma tumors could grow without a recognized driver. One was that an undetected genetic change was activating RAS signaling. Another was that a different mechanism allowed the cells to divide without relying on RAS. A third was that some tumors had acquired characteristics of another cell type and no longer behaved like typical lung adenocarcinomas. Theorizer helped turn his broad question about unexplained tumor growth into specific hypotheses he could investigate in molecular data.

blocks.text: Devarakonda and the Asta team investigated these theories with AutoDiscovery, which writes and runs code to test hypotheses against datasets. Devarakonda used The Cancer Genome Atlas, a public collection of molecular data from tumors, to compare genetic changes, gene activity, and protein measurements in cancers with and without recognized drivers. He also examined data from laboratory-grown cancer cells to identify genes needed for growth or survival.

blocks.text: AutoDiscovery suggested that disruption of the DREAM complex, a group of proteins that normally keeps cell division in check, might help explain the tumors’ growth. Devarakonda had not initially focused on this mechanism. Working with the Asta team, he compared RAS activity with how strongly genes normally controlled by the complex were switched on.

blocks.text: Follow-up work with data from laboratory-grown cancer cells gave Devarakonda preliminary support for the hypothesis that some cancers with low RAS activity may depend on CDK2, a protein involved in cell division. If those cells depend on CDK2, blocking the protein could offer a way to slow or stop their growth.

blocks.text: Lecoq evaluated an early version of Theorizer on VIP interneurons, brain cells that suppress the activity of other neurons. Their targets include inhibitory cells that normally dampen activity in the surrounding circuit. Suppressing those cells can allow nearby neurons to respond more strongly.

blocks.text: An anomaly in Peru’s climate data

inlines.text: An anomaly in Peru’s climate data

blocks.text: At the International Potato Center (CIP) in Peru, Piero Palacios, a data scientist and statistical specialist, develops tools to help researchers analyze complex datasets. Henry Juarez, CIP’s systems and data management officer, works on agricultural data and research into the conservation of native potato varieties.

inlines.text: At the International Potato Center (CIP) in Peru, Piero Palacios, a data scientist and statistical specialist, develops tools to help researchers analyze complex datasets. Henry Juarez, CIP’s systems and data management officer, works on agricultural data and research into the conservation of native potato varieties.

blocks.text: Palacios and Juarez wanted to extend the dew-point record in PISCO, a dataset that uses weather-station observations to estimate climate conditions across Peru. A longer record would supply missing inputs for agricultural models, including those used to approximate crop water requirements.

inlines.text: Palacios and Juarez wanted to extend the dew-point record in PISCO, a dataset that uses weather-station observations to estimate climate conditions across Peru. A longer record would supply missing inputs for agricultural models, including those used to approximate crop water requirements.

blocks.text: PISCO’s dew-point records end in 2016, while its minimum-temperature records continue through 2020. Palacios and Juarez used the overlapping historical data to estimate dew point for the missing four years, but some reconstructed values exceeded 35°C – implausibly high daily dew points for the affected areas – and clustered in November.

blocks.text: Palacios and Juarez used Theorizer to generate possible explanations for the unusually high November dew points. One proposed explanation was a rise in humidity as the Amazon shifts from dry to wet conditions. Testing that seasonal explanation against their data ruled it out for the study area, but it prompted Palacios and Juarez to investigate how the original climate record had been constructed.

blocks.text: “Having a specific, falsifiable mechanism on the table is what drove us to measure the November spike by distance from the stations in the historical record,” Palacios and Juarez say. “That was an analysis we had no particular reason to run while the anomaly was merely unexplained, and it is the analysis that produced the actual answer.”

inlines.text: A century of potato diversity

blocks.text: Vilma Hualla, a data management specialist at CIP, studies the diversity of native potato varieties in the Andes. She and her colleagues are examining historical records and household surveys spanning a century in Paucartambo, in Peru’s Cusco region.

blocks.text: Hualla used AutoDiscovery to compare the varieties recorded in the six periods. In most transitions, more varieties entered the records than left them, but the transition from 1941–60 to 1961–80 was an exception: more varieties disappeared from the records than appeared for the first time.

blocks.text: Hualla then used Theorizer to generate explanations for the drop in recorded varieties, drawing on relevant literature and reviewing which hypotheses to pursue or reject. In their draft report, Hualla and her colleagues discuss Peru’s 1969 agrarian reform and the associated shift toward commercial production as one possible cause of a decline in native varieties. They also consider whether differences in the historical sources could account for an apparent loss of varieties in the records.
